rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests the baseline performance of a simple rna_only model with singleprofile and pca_n2000 encoder. It clarifies the impact of using PCA for RNA representation and isolates the effect of modalities. This is the best first step to establish a baseline for comparison with more complex configurations.

The existing evidence shows that the baseline (config_001) achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy with RNA-only, single-profile data. This experiment tests the impact of switching to multiprofile data while using avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile setting. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether multiprofile data improves performance, a key design choice, without changing other factors like encoders or fusion methods.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002) outperform singleprofile (config_001). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated model) in the multiprofile setting improves performance, isolating the impact of representation choice. It balances exploration (testing a new encoder) with exploitation (building on the multiprofile advantage).

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings and scvi_n200 RNA encoder significantly improve accuracy (config_005: 0.650). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool (config_005) to transformer (config_006) further improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It builds on the promising direction of multiprofile + scvi_n200 while exploring a key design choice with minimal additional complexity.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings and scvi_n200 encoder improve RNA-only accuracy. This experiment tests whether using transformer aggregation with pca_n2000 (instead of avgpool) further improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It clarifies if transformer aggregation is critical for RNA-only models, providing insight into design choices without changing multiple factors simultaneously.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile settings (configs 002, 005-006) outperform singleprofile (config 001). The best RNA-only accuracy is 0.652970 (config 006) using scvi_n200 with transformer aggregation. This experiment tests scgpt encoder (a more complex representation) with multiprofile and avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of encoder choice while maintaining multiprofile (exploiting prior evidence of its benefit). It balances exploration of encoder architecture vs exploitation of multiprofile's proven advantage.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and avgpool aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether adding image data (resnet50) to this strong RNA-only baseline improves performance, isolating the effect of multimodal fusion. It balances exploitation of the top RNA-only setup with exploration of multimodal potential, addressing a key design choice without changing multiple factors simultaneously.

Existing evidence shows that rna_only models with scvi_n200 encoder, multiprofile, and transformer aggregation achieve the highest accuracy (0.652970). This experiment tests whether combining these components with multimodal data (resnet50 image encoder) and weighted fusion can improve performance, isolating the effect of image modality and fusion method. It balances exploitation of known strong components with exploration of multimodal potential.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieve the highest accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l image encoder while keeping RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion unchanged. It isolates the effect of image encoder choice, a critical design decision, to determine if the ViT-L architecture improves performance further. This balances exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of a key hyperparameter.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039) achieve high performance. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 (used in config_039) with scgpt, while keeping the image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), aggregation (transformer), and fusion (weighted) unchanged, can further improve accuracy. This isolates the effect of the RNA encoder choice, a critical design decision, and leverages the strong prior evidence for transformer/weighted configurations.
